system.summary: Book code: a token a/b points to line a, letter b of one page of a book (letters counted without spaces); a letter can be written with any cell that holds it. Digits point to the digit characters at the start of the key page's lines, which seem to be a numbered list of titles (37 IDYLLS OF THE KING, 7? ENOCH ARDEN, ?8 FRIENDSHIP ...). A dash separates words. Two pages were in use: 'old code page 14' and 'new code last page'.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct tokens in the 28 runs (439 tokens, docs/_check_profile.py --measure transcription.txt --digits --drop-first). Doubled letters take two different cells (HARR 2/9 3/4; MILWAUKEE 1/13 2/3). The new-code grid has 112 cells from the Bureau decodes; the old-code page 14 grid has 27 cells from one decode (A14), where numbers are spelt out. The book is not identified.

prior_solution.where: The Bureau of Investigation's own 'Decode:' lines and pencil glosses on the same typed copies (1920-21) decode 16 of the 28 runs (15 new code, 1 old code). The catalogue entry already noted them. No printed decipherment was looked for beyond the catalogue's check: Draper (1957) and the other three parts of case 202600 were not checked.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 678) and the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the scans, transcribed, rebuilt the grid, ran the tests and verified. No target-specific human intervention.
tools: decode.py (grid from the Bureau decodes, leave-one-run-out test, controls, digit-model test, decoding)
PDF text layer scan for fraction runs (working script, not included)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT); a vision-capable language model for the transcription

solution.what: Downloaded M1085-940A/B/C from the NARA record (naId 369272950) and scanned the PDF text layer of all 3,222 pages for line/letter runs; every flagged page was viewed. 940C has no runs; C1085 was checked by eye (its fraction-like strings are dates).
Transcribed 28 runs on 14 typed pages (439 tokens) with their clear context. Handwritten pages have no text layer and were not searched, so the catalogue's 77 runs could not be reproduced.

Aligned the Bureau's own decodes token by token: a/b = line a, letter b of one page, letters counted without spaces (on line 2 the Bureau's words give letters 3-9 as ENOCHAR, contiguous; the struck typed 'arden' on A0880 fits 2/8-2/12).

First digit rule: a digit is written by the first letter of its English name (1=O, 2/3=T, 4/5=F, 6/7=S, 8=E). It fits the Bureau's numbers, but not the cells: digits only ever use letter positions 1-2 and never share a cell between 4/5, 6/7 or 2/3.

Digit-character model: a digit token points to a digit printed at the start of a key line (a numbered list of titles). All 40 digit tokens in Bureau-decoded runs sit at positions 1-2, against 1 of 297 letter tokens (a slip); no cell is used for two digits.

Independent re-reading of the scans and an independent script: found that A11, A13 and A939 carry Bureau decodes (the first pass had them as new readings), A11 line 2 is 11/2 5/1 3/2, and the signature of A11 has no address (so 148 is the Bureau's, not an independent check). Leave-one-run-out on 11 runs: 216 right, 1 wrong, 31 unseen.

Redo: re-read A887 runs (2) and (3) on enlarged crops (run 2 now complete; in run 3 W = 14/3, M = 27/34, AVE = 10/7 18/11 11/5, plus SUPERIOR) and the A886 member run (last token 4/5, not 4/3: [..]ERIC).

Grid from the Bureau decodes only, leave one run out over 15 new-code runs: letters 251 right, 4 wrong, 42 unseen; digits 34 right, 1 wrong, 5 unseen. All misses are clashes inside the Bureau's own decodes (5/14 Y vs U, 1/2 I vs 7, 26/30 L vs Z). Controls: shuffled grid 4.7% right (500 repetitions); grid shifted one line 3 right, 178 wrong; one letter along 13 right, 160 wrong.

Read the runs without a Bureau decode with the full grid: S. RUBIN (B494), MINOR (A493), MAY 12 (A527), 1148 S. 8[th] St. (A888), [..]ERIC Sahlin (A886.3); in part AT[?]OOD and U[?]P / [?]P (A706). Corrected the Bureau's SOVRYS to SOV. RUS. (Soviet Russia).
Identify the key book from the grid rows (line prefixes and titles: Idylls of the King, Enoch Arden, Friendship, Socialis[m], Poe...). Not identified; no search of book lists was made.
Only the catalogue's own prior-art check (repo lists, NARA READMEs). Draper (1957) and the other three parts of case 202600 on roll 940 were not checked.

texts.label: Names, addresses and telegram signatures: A0011-A0015, A0880, A0886-A0888
texts.note: Names, street addresses, an organizer's official name and the National Office's telegram signatures. The code holds no sentences on these pages. A0880 and A0888 have no Bureau decode; the others are checked against the Bureau's.
texts.summary: Addresses of party agents and contacts in Wisconsin, Ohio, Arizona, Philadelphia and the Northwest (bundle, telegraph and literature addresses), an organizer's official name (Paul Stockman) and the N.O.'s telegram signature (new code: ARDEN, resting partly on a struck typed word).

texts.label: Coded words in clear sentences: A0493, A0527, A0939, B0494
texts.summary: A district knows nothing of an application 'for MINOR'; unity-convention delegates are to be elected by MAY 12 (1921); members of the I.W.[W.] distribute leaflets, and a route is proposed for the magazine Soviet Russia; S. Rubin is put forward as the new district organizer in the Milwaukee district.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, reviewed against the scans)
reading_review.note: Every coded word has a value and fits its clear sentence: 24 of 24 tokens. Who MINOR is stays open; that is a question of identity, not of reading.

texts.label: A0706, report of Grey, D.O. 12, 23 Mar 1921
texts.summary: A delegate of the 'P A C' (AT[?]OOD, likely Atwood) calls a joint meeting of the other party and the writer's district committee; a joint committee of two members of the writer's party (U[?]P) and three of the other ([?]P) is to issue a paper before a convention to be held within two months.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, reviewed against the scans)
reading_review.note: The clear sentences read; the coded words have holes at 5/29 and 5/12 in every occurrence. The typed 'and' between two tokens is left out and two typing slips are normalised. 11 of 17 tokens have a value.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 678). Mostly names and addresses. The decipherment of 1920-21 is the Bureau's own; what is added is the grid and its test, the digit model, the Bureau's slips (SOVRYS for SOV. RUS.; the OHIO token), and the runs the Bureau left undecoded.
